extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners using recurrence plots and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) for nonlinear time series and dynamical systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and quantitative measures for constructing, parameterising, interpreting and using recurrence plots (RPs), cross- and joint-RPs, and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) on time series and spatial data to characterise dynamical systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of the threshold ε
rubrics_metrics.description: The neighbourhood radius ε that defines recurrence points in an RP is a crucial parameter: too small → almost no recurrences; too large → artefacts and tangential motion (consecutive points counted as recurrences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules of thumb and procedures given: (a) few percent of maximum phase-space diameter; (b) do not exceed 10% of mean or maximum phase-space diameter; (c) choose ε so recurrence point density RR ≈ 1% for non-stationary data; (d) choose ε > 5·σ_obs (five times observational noise std) to preserve signal structures; (e) choose ε by seeking a scaling region in recurrence point density; (f) for (quasi-)periodic data, choose ε minimising β(ε) = |Nn(ε)/Np(ε) − Nn(ε)| where Np = number of significant diagonal peaks and Nn = average number of neighbours; (g) choose ε as the RR-th percentile of the cumulative distribution of pairwise distances (fixed RR); (h) alternatively fix number of neighbours per point (variable ε_i) to preserve local RR. Notes: all dynamical invariants from RPs are strictly valid only as ε → 0; noise can bias ε selection and the β(ε) criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of norm for neighbourhood
rubrics_metrics.description: The chosen vector norm (L1, L2, L∞) defines neighbourhood shape and thus how many points are considered neighbours for a given ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: L∞ (maximum norm) is often used (computationally faster, analytically convenient) and yields the most neighbours for fixed ε; L2 (Euclidean) yields an intermediate number; L1 yields the fewest. Choice affects RP texture and must be reported/considered when comparing RPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-space reconstruction (embedding dimension m and time delay τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: When only a scalar observable is available, reconstruct phase space by delay embedding using parameters m and τ to form vectors ˆx_i = [u_i, u_{i+τ}, …, u_{i+(m−1)τ}].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose embedding dimension m (e.g., via false nearest neighbours) and delay τ (e.g., via auto-correlation or mutual information). Takens' theorem (and extensions) justify reconstruction if m ≥ 2D2 + 1; incorrect embedding can create spurious RP structures (e.g., mirror diagonals) and bias invariant estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding tangential motion and consecutive-point artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consecutive samples on a trajectory (tangential motion) can be erroneously included in neighbourhoods, producing artificially thick/long diagonal structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent by choosing ε and embedding so that neighbourhoods don't primarily include temporally adjacent points, or by applying Theiler window/time-exclusion to ignore recurrences within short time lags. Recognise tangential motion as a source of overestimated diagonals and spurious predictability measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typology of large-scale RP patterns for interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale RP appearance (typology) indicates broad system behaviour: homogeneous, periodic/quasi-periodic, drift (non-stationarity), disrupted (abrupt changes/extreme events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual inspection to classify: homogeneous → stationary with short relaxation times; periodic → diagonal, checkerboard structures; drift → RP fades away from LOI; disrupted → white areas/bands indicate abrupt dynamics or extreme events. This guides further quantitative analysis and parameter choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of small-scale RP texture (dots, diagonals, verticals, bowed lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local line-like and point structures encode specific dynamical features: isolated points, diagonal lines, vertical/horizontal lines, bowed lines each have distinct meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single isolated points: rare states or strong fluctuations (not uniquely noise). Diagonal lines: segments of trajectory evolving similarly for l time steps → relate to predictability and entropy; vertical/horizontal lines: trapping/laminar states/intermittency (state changes slowly); bowed lines: non-constant slope indicating local time-scale transformations. Use these interpretations to select RQA measures and to diagnose embedding/time-scaling issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of diagonal-line based measures (predictability metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal-line statistics quantify how long trajectory segments stay close (predictability). Key quantities include histogram P(ε,l), p(ε,l), average diagonal length L, longest diagonal L_max, and measures derived from those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minimum diagonal length l_min to exclude trivial short lines. DET (determinism) = ratio of recurrence points forming diagonals ≥ l_min to all recurrence points; DETτ and diagonal-wise RRτ can probe periodicities. The inverse of the longest diagonal (excluding LOI) is linked to largest Lyapunov exponent; diagonal-length distributions relate to correlation entropy K2. Choose l_min and ε carefully; tangential motion inflates diagonal lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of vertical-line based measures (laminarity metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical (and horizontal) lines quantify trapping and laminar phases (intermittency). Statistics include number/lengths of vertical lines, laminarity LAM, trapping time (TT), V_max and v_min.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define minimal vertical length v_min to exclude noise. LAM = fraction of recurrence points forming vertical lines ≥ v_min; trapping time is average vertical-line length. Use these to detect intermittency, laminar states, and regime changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence density measures (recurrence rate RR and RRτ)
rubrics_metrics.description: RR (recurrence rate) is the percentage/density of recurrence points in the RP; RRτ is the recurrence rate along τ-th diagonal (diagonal-wise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RR is a basic normalisation and descriptive measure; fix RR or use percentile-based ε to compare across datasets. RRτ (and its peaks) helps detect periodicities and choose ε for periodic signals. Beware non-stationarity: fixed RR may mask changes in dynamics unless applied locally or with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinism (DET) and related diagonal-based indices
rubrics_metrics.description: DET quantifies the proportion of recurrence points forming diagonal lines (≥ l_min), interpreted as amount of deterministic structure or predictability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High DET ≈ deterministic/repetitive dynamics; low DET ≈ stochasticity. Use DET together with RR to avoid misinterpretation (e.g., high RR with low DET indicates many isolated recurrences). Compute DETτ to study periodic components along specific lags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divergence (DIV) and relation to Lyapunov exponents
rubrics_metrics.description: Divergence (often defined as inverse of the longest diagonal L_max) is related to exponential divergence of trajectories and thus to the largest Lyapunov exponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate Lyapunov-like behaviour from DIV with caution: finite-size effects, noise, ε choice, and embedding affect estimates. Use as qualitative indicator and, when automated, combine with surrogate testing or other invariant estimators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy measures derived from line length distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entropy (e.g., Renyi or Shannon-like entropy of diagonal/vertical line length distributions) quantifies complexity/unpredictability of line structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute entropy of diagonal lengths (line-length histogram P(ε,l)) to characterise complexity; higher entropy typically indicates more heterogeneous line-length distribution and richer dynamics. Interpret alongside DET and RR; require adequate data length and appropriate l_min to get meaningful statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence-time based measures and periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrence times (first/second type T(1), T(2), phase period T_ph, T_rec) summarise temporal intervals between recurrences and can reveal periodicities and characteristic timescales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate recurrence period and distributions of recurrence times; check for exponential or Poisson-like distributions for mixing/hyperbolic systems. Relate observed recurrence-time statistics to theoretical expectations (e.g., exponential limit laws for hyperbolic systems) and to physical timescales in the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of minimum line lengths (l_min, v_min)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum lengths l_min (diagonals) and v_min (verticals) are preprocessing thresholds that determine which short structures are considered in RQA measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set l_min and v_min to exclude trivial short lines arising from noise and from single-point recurrences; report chosen values. Sensitivity analyses recommended because RQA indices depend on these cut-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and comparison strategies (fixed RR vs fixed neighbours)
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare RPs across datasets, one can either fix ε globally, fix recurrence rate RR (percentile-based ε), or fix number of neighbours per point (adaptive ε_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed RR or fixed-number-of-neighbours preserves comparability but have trade-offs: fixed ε is simplest but may yield different RR across series; fixing RR standardises density but may require different ε per dataset; fixing neighbours gives local adaptivity and is useful for inhomogeneous data. State the method used when comparing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation and limits of dynamical invariants from RPs
rubrics_metrics.description: RPs can be used to estimate dynamical invariants: correlation entropy K2, correlation dimension D2, point-wise dimension, and generalised mutual information indices I_q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates require careful parameter choice and are valid in the limit ε → 0 and sufficient data length. Embedding and noise influence estimates; use proper scaling regions, surrogate tests, and complementary invariant estimation methods. Automatised K2 estimation algorithms are available but must be validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross recurrence plots (CRP) and joint recurrence plots (JRP) for multivariate analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: CRP compares two trajectories in the same phase space (CR matrix) to reveal shared states/time-relations; JRP uses joint recurrence of multiple systems to analyse multivariate synchrony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CRP to detect time-lagged similarity and to compute CRP-specific measures (CRP asymmetry, symmetry indices q(τ), Q(τ)). Use joint RPs for multivariate synchronisation detection and to compute joint recurrence-based indices (JC, JP_R). Ensure comparable normalisation/embedding and appropriate thresholds for each series when constructing CRP/JRP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronization detection and Line of Synchronization (LOS) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: RP-based tools can detect and quantify different synchronisation forms (complete synchronisation CS, phase synchronisation PS, generalized synchronisation GS) using CRP/JRP features and the LOS (distorted main diagonal) fitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect synchronisation transitions by analysing CRP asymmetry, LOS slope and fit algorithms, joint recurrence synchronization indices, and recurrence-based surrogate testing. LOS fitting algorithms can align time scales between series. Use twin or recurrence-based surrogates to test significance of synchrony findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrogate-data testing and twin-surrogates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recurrence-based surrogates (including twin surrogates) to test hypotheses like presence of synchronisation or nonlinearity in data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate surrogates that preserve certain recurrence structures (or other statistics) to form null distributions for RQA/synchronization measures. Twin surrogates preserve recurrences and are recommended for testing complex synchronisation hypotheses; report surrogate generation method and significance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of embedding and parameter choice on invariants and RP structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding (m, τ), threshold ε, norm, l_min/v_min, and data length strongly affect RP structures and any derived invariants/indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensitivity analyses for embedding and ε; check for embedding artifacts (e.g., diagonals perpendicular to LOI indicating wrong embedding). When estimating invariants (D2, K2) prefer multiple methods and report parameter-dependence and scaling ranges used for estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of noise and robustness considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational and dynamical noise distort RP structures and RQA measures; noise can obliterate line structures or create spurious recurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate by choosing ε larger than noise level (ε > 5·σ_obs), using surrogates to test significance, and understanding that some denoising criteria (e.g., β(ε) minimisation) may underestimate ε under noise. Evaluate robustness of measures under added noise and consider preprocessing/filtering carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for spatial data and multivariate/spatial recurrence plots
rubrics_metrics.description: The RP concept extends to spatial data (spatial recurrence plots) and multivariate time series (multivariate RPs, multivariate RQA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt neighbourhood definitions and parameters to spatial contexts; use multivariate RPs to capture interactions among several observables (e.g., multivariate recurrence plots and joint measures). Consider domain-specific normalisation and interpretation for spatial applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recurrence histograms and probability distributions (P(ε,l), p(ε,l), pc(ε,l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Histograms of line lengths and recurrence distances provide empirical distributions used in many RQA measures and in estimates of entropies and invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute and inspect P(ε,l), p(ε,l) (probability of lines of exactly or at least length l), and their cumulative forms when estimating entropies or K2. Choose binning and statistical treatments appropriate to data length; use these distributions to compute mean line lengths, L_max, entropy, and related metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical algorithmic and computational guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical procedures and algorithms are provided (e.g., LOS fitting, reconstruction from RP, twin surrogates, automation of K2 estimation), and code/toolboxes (CRP toolbox for Matlab) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use implemented, tested tools (e.g., CRP toolbox) to avoid reimplementation errors. When automating invariant estimation (K2 etc.), validate outputs against known examples and check sensitivity to parameters. Document algorithm versions and parameter settings used in analyses.
